newsitem.title: USA: Texas power prices up with some calls for cold.
newsitem.headline: Texas power prices up with some calls for cold.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) climbed again Tuesday with some forecasts calling for continued cold weather in the north through Wednesday, industry sources said.

Forecasts called for temperatures below normal in northern Texas and above normal in the south Wednesday and Thursday, while temperatures were called to be well above normal Friday through Sunday, especially in the north and west.
But other forecasts called for continued cold through much of the state, and the mixed predictions had ERCOT traders quoting next-day power over a wide price range.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Wednesday delivery was pegged at $30.00-33.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $27.00-29.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Some firm next day peak power had been offered as high as $40, although sources said they had not heard of any business being done at that level.
One source reported trading a 24-hour block of ERCOT peak power for Wednesday at $30.75, although the trade was not confirmed.
Non-firm on peak power for Wednesday was notionally said to be higher at $27.00-30.00 from a notional assessment at $25.00-27.00 on Monday.
Firm off-peak Wednesday ERCOT deliveries were assessed higher at $18.00-20.00 from $13.00-15.00 on Monday, although trade was said to be very thin.
Non firm off peak power was notionally pegged higher at $15.00-17.00 from $10.00-13.00 on Monday, the sources said.
February ERCOT peak power was assessed higher at $27.00-27.60 from a Monday notional assessment at $25.00-26.00 per MWh.
July/August ERCOT was talked at $24.75-25.10 per MWh, the sources said.
